added_lines: 30th sunday in ordinary time 25th october 2026 one question, one answer: two sides, same coin another week, another trap. last sunday they came with a coin. this week a lawyer comes with a question: which commandment is the greatest? jesus does not hesitate. love the lord your god with all your heart, all your soul, all your mind. then, though nobody asked, he adds a second and says it is like the first: love your neighbour as yourself. on these two hang the whole law and the prophets. think back to that coin. every coin has two sides, heads and tails, but nobody has ever spent one side of a coin. it is one piece of metal or it is nothing. that is what jesus is saying about love. love of god is one side. love of neighbour is the other. try to separate them and you are left holding something worthless. you cannot love the god you have never seen while ignoring the neighbour you see every day. and you cannot truly love the neighbour without the god whose image that neighbour bears. that is the link. last week jesus asked whose image was on the coin. we said that we bear god’s image. so does the stranger, the widow, the orphan, the man whose cloak is held in pledge. the first reading is blunt about it: give the cloak back by sunset, because it is all he has to sleep in. god’s compassion lands in practical places, in coins and cloaks. st paul tells the thessalonians that their faith is known everywhere. not because of their preaching, but because people sawhow they lived. their faith had two sides, but it was never two-faced. like the coin, it was solid and the same. loving god is what we do in church. loving neighbour is how the world knows we mean it. two sides. same coin. spend it well. fr sean announcements sion mills

a short reflection on today’s gospel matthew 21:15-21 in today’s gospel jesus tells us to “repay to caesar what belongs to caesar and to god what belongs to god.” his words invite us to reflect on our priorities, our responsibilities and the place god holds in our lives. while we have duties to our families, communities and society, our relationship with god must always remain at the centre. giving to god what belongs to god means more than attending mass or saying our prayers. it means living our faith through love, kindness, forgiveness and compassion. when we care for the vulnerable, support those in need and reach out to the lonely, we make god's love visible through our actions. in the busyness of everyday life, we can sometimes forget to make time for god. today's gospel reminds us that our possessions and achievements should never take his place in our hearts. what matters most is how we use our gifts and blessings to serve god and others. as we reflect on today's gospel, let us ask ourselves: am i putting god first? am i using my gifts for the good of others? do my words and actions reflect the love of christ? may we have the courage to put god first, the generosity to serve others and the humility to recognise his presence in everyone we meet. lord, help us to give you what truly belongs to you: our hearts, our lives and our love. guide us to serve others with kindness and generosity, and may everything we say and do bring glory to your holy name. amen. prayer for vocations to the priesthood : st paul could have written this passage from today's second reading to our seminarians and to the men discerning their vocation: "we know, brothers, that god loves you and that you have been chosen, because when we brought the good news to you, it came to you not only as words, but as power and the holy spirit and as utter conviction." mission sunday 2026 – one in christ, united in mission. mission sunday, celebrated today, sunday 18th october 2026, invites us to renew our commitment to sharing the good news of jesus christ with people throughout the world. it is a special opportunity to pray for missionaries and the communities they serve, and to support their work through our generosity. across the world, missionaries bring hope, comfort and practical help to those in need, often in challenging circumstances. as a parish community, we are reminded that mission begins with each of us. through our prayers, kindness and willingness to serve others, we can make christ’s love visible in our homes, our parish and the wider world. may this mission sunday inspire us to be joyful witnesses to the gospel, sharing god’s love with everyone we meet. the st mass with anointing of the sick will be celebrated at st eugene’s cathedral on tuesday 20th october at 7.30pm. this mass is to give thanks to god for positive mental health and to pray for those who are struggling with mental health issues and those who care for them. our lady, untier of knots novena - the novena to our lady, untier of knots continues after the 7.30pm mass on thursdays, in st eugene’s cathedral, concluding on thursday 26th november. this novena reminds us that sin never entangled our lady, and that christ gave us his mother as our lady, untier of knots. through this devotion, we entrust our personal “knots” to her loving care - learning to let go and allowing her to gently untie what binds us. all are welcome to join in prayer and reflection during this special time of grace. parish pilgrimage to rome, loreto, cascia & assisi, italy – 24-31 may 2027 – fr
